newsitem.title: USA: Kodak forecasts future sales from abroad.
newsitem.headline: Kodak forecasts future sales from abroad.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. expects 75 percent to 80 percent of its revenues to come from outside the United States in 10 years, Kodak's Chief Executive Officer George Fisher said late Tuesday.
The current percentage of revenues from outside the United States is a little more than 50 percent.
At that time, half the company's revenues will be from digital products, he said in answers to questions at the New York Financial Writers' Association 1997 annual awards dinner.
Kodak has said previously that digitalization - or the ability to take an existing image and transfer it into digital mode - is a key part of its strategy.
It said it had $1.5 billion in sales of digital products last year, an increase of 25 percent over 1995.
Asked also about Fuji as a competitor, Fisher said: "By all reasonable expectations, we should walk away from them."
